conclusion: Automatic sensitivity makes a substantial difference in one corrected Craftsman no-strip tape-measure control. The other 89 tool-on-white-sheet views are exactly unchanged. This is occasional failure recovery, not a broad improvement to ordinary outlines.
findings: Both columns already use TEED. This comparison changes only the edge-threshold selection; the earlier large improvement over color/GrabCut came from TEED itself.

Only substantial change: Craftsman tape measure without the reference strip, exact perspective-corrected browser crop. The fixed threshold fragments the silhouette into two regions and excludes part of the body; Auto selects 0.57 and produces one complete outer silhouette. Fresh detection is 796 → 897 ms in this rerun.

All other 89 in-scope views are byte-identical in dense and displayed outlines. There is no additional large improvement to highlight in the Wolfbox, Gerber, calipers, single Wiha drivers or other tested tools. The newly prepared crops of the same tape-measure photo also stay unchanged; the benefit depends on the failing crop/resampling.

The primary review uses 36 actual tool-on-white-Pocketry-sheet photos, producing 88 corpus views plus the two exact browser controls. Eight tray/packaging/mixed-scene views are retained in a separate context report and excluded from this comparison.

The loose Wiha group stays fragmented and has an existing joined pair of handles. It remains a diagnostic case rather than the adoption criterion. One-tool crops are included, but four of five still fall back with extra fragments in this photo.

The reviewed single-tool hook and bit points remain covered. Existing transparent-part failures and grouped-tool limitations are unchanged. Three deterministic before/after/cached samples per evaluated view are retained; no model inference was rerun for this report-scope correction.

photos.0: The clip is present; the corrected-view check lies about 2.2 px outside the contour. Treat this as a small existing localization mismatch, not new feature loss.
photos.5: The crop includes sheet printing and the recognized aid. Both revisions fall back and can return extra paper/printing contours. This is an existing selection/background limitation.
photos.7: The two tips remain separate in both group views. Individual transparent-tip crops remain sensitive to orientation and crop context; one original crop misses much of the clear hub. Before and after are identical.
photos.18: The ratchet and loaded tray remain separate. The tiny loose metal bit is missed by both revisions. The separate ratchet crop returns one outline.
photos.19: Context test of a loaded printed tray. Extra sheet/wood boundaries are present before and after; contour count is not the count of loose tools.
photos.22: The white/translucent plunger has an inward-folding boundary and misses a mid-body probe in both revisions. Auto does not correct this white-on-white case.
photos.26: The fine hook near-end point is retained in both dense and displayed outlines, in both original and corrected views. Before and after are identical.
photos.30: The reviewed bit near-end point is retained in both dense and displayed outlines. Before and after are identical.
photos.31: Diagnostic group: eight original / nine corrected shapes; the first two handles are already joined, the first shaft is missed and other shafts fragment. Header/footer printing lies close to the tool ends. Roomier individual selections retain complete tools, but four still fall back with extra fragments; only the fifth gives one clean outline. Auto makes no change.
photos.32: Diagnostic retail packaging, not isolated loose tools. Near/touching packages and paper/wood edges are included in existing merged/extra contours. No new merging from Auto.
photos.33: Diagnostic wide packaging scene with overlapping/nearby cases. The combined exterior is unchanged; this is the slowest view and is not used to judge isolated-tool adoption.
photos.34: Early sheet version is unrecognized for current paper correction. Original-pixel detection is included and unchanged.
photos.36: The body and cone remain two separate shapes in both group views. Individual crops include the complete objects with surrounding paper. All before/after outlines are unchanged.
photos.38: Early sheet version is unrecognized for current paper correction. Original-pixel detection is included and unchanged.

cases.browser-no-strip-corrected-control: Positive control: exact pixels from the earlier compiled-browser workflow. Two fragments belong to one tape measure. Auto joins them into one supported silhouette without changing the slider. This is the only changed result in this review.
cases.browser-strip-corrected-control: Exact prior browser control. The recognized strip/estimated hidden-edge behavior stays unchanged.
